title: jasper-deploy jrs.config.json
description: The skill's local connection config (jrs.config.json in the skill root, gitignored). All jasper-deploy scripts resolve credentials in order: script params -> env JRS_URL/JRS_USER/JRS_PASS (and JR_LIB_DIR) -> this file. Copy jrs.config.example.json to jrs.config.json and fill it in. Unknown keys are allowed.

The password may come from `password` (plaintext), `passwordCommand` (a PowerShell command whose stdout is the secret, so nothing plaintext lives on disk), or $env:JRS_PASS / -Password. At least one must be resolvable at run time.

serverUrl.description: Base URL of the JasperReports Server, e.g. http://localhost:8081/jasperserver-pro (no trailing slash; scripts trim one anyway). Overridden by -ServerUrl or $env:JRS_URL.

user.description: JRS user for HTTP Basic auth, e.g. superuser. Overridden by -User or $env:JRS_USER.

password.description: Plaintext password for the JRS user. Overridden by -Password or $env:JRS_PASS. Keep this file gitignored. Prefer passwordCommand or $env:JRS_PASS to avoid a plaintext secret on disk.

passwordCommand.description: Alternative to `password`: a PowerShell command whose stdout is the password (used only if password/env are not set), so the secret can live in a vault/keychain instead of this file. Windows example: "(Get-StoredCredential -Target jrs).GetNetworkCredential().Password". macOS example: "security find-generic-password -s jrs -w". Any command that prints the secret works.

dataSourceUri.description: Optional default datasource repository URI used as a fallback when a script's -DataSourceUri is not supplied, e.g. /datasources/postgis_34_sample.

jrLibDir.description: Path to the JasperReports 7 runtime jar directory used for local compile/render. Windows: C:\path\to\jasperreports-lib; macOS/Linux: /absolute/path/to/jasperreports-lib. Overridden by -LibDir or $env:JR_LIB_DIR; scripts error with guidance if no source supplies a value.

chartCustomizerJar.description: Optional. Absolute path to actian-chart-customizers.jar inside your JRS webapp's WEB-INF/lib, used only by doctor.ps1 to confirm the bar-gradient chart customizer is on the live classpath. Prefer jrsWebappDir (doctor derives WEB-INF/lib from it). Install-/OS-specific; on Windows doctor.ps1 falls back to the standard C:\Jaspersoft install path when both are unset.

jrsWebappDir.description: Optional. Absolute path of the deployed JRS webapp directory on THIS machine (the exploded war, e.g. C:\Jaspersoft\jasperreports-server-10.0.0\apache-tomcat\webapps\jasperserver-pro or /opt/jasperserver/apache-tomcat/webapps/jasperserver-pro). Used only by doctor.ps1: (a) <dir>/WEB-INF/lib/actian-chart-customizers.jar is checked for presence and its SHA-256 compared with the bundled chart_customizers jar; (b) <dir>/META-INF/context.xml (or WEB-INF/js.jdbc.properties) is parsed for the repository jdbc URL so the REAL metadata-DB port is reported and cross-checked against repoDb. Leave unset on a machine that only talks to a remote server.

environments.description: Optional named environment profiles, selected with a script's -Env parameter or $env:JRS_ENV (e.g. -Env prod, or promote.ps1 -FromEnv stage -ToEnv prod). Each profile may carry any of the top-level connection keys (serverUrl, user, password, passwordCommand, dataSourceUri); keys a profile omits fall through to the top level. While a profile is active the JRS_URL/JRS_USER/JRS_PASS process env vars are ignored so a stale shell export cannot silently retarget a named environment; explicit script params still override.

repoDb.description: Optional. The JRS repository *metadata* PostgreSQL database (the bundled instance, NOT the reporting datasource), used read-only by report_usage.ps1 for access-event/usage reporting and checked by doctor.ps1. On this install the live metadata DB listens on port 5433; a stale decoy jasperserver DB exists on :5432 -- do not point this at it. Password comes from $env:PGPASSWORD or a .pgpass entry, never this file.
